issues.legal_issue: A conviction for abduction cannot be sustained where the eyewitness accounts are unreliable and the prosecution fails to establish the accused persons’ participation beyond reasonable doubt.
A murder conviction based on circumstantial evidence cannot be sustained when the circumstances linking the accused to the crime are unproved and the chain of evidence is incomplete.
An appellate court may reverse an acquittal only when the trial court’s view is unsustainable, rather than merely because another view of the evidence is possible.
Motive alone cannot establish guilt without proof of the foundational facts and ingredients of the offence.
A post-mortem opinion on the time of death may be accepted where no credible evidence contradicts it.
